title: Understanding the Elbow Method
text: The elbow method is a visual tool used to determine the optimal number of clusters in k-Means clustering. It involves plotting the sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned cluster center as a function of the number of clusters. What do you think happens to this sum as the number of clusters increases?

hintAnswer: A line with a distinct bend or 'elbow'
title: Visualizing the Elbow Method
text: Imagine plotting the sum of squared distances for different numbers of clusters. What shape do you expect the plot to take if you were to draw a line through the points?
choices: A line with a distinct bend or 'elbow'

title: Interpreting the Elbow
text: The 'elbow' in the plot represents a point where adding more clusters doesn't significantly reduce the sum of squared distances. Why might this point be a good choice for the number of clusters?

hintAnswer: It balances between minimizing the sum of squared distances and avoiding overfitting.
title: Choosing the Optimal k
text: Why is the 'elbow' point considered optimal in k-Means clustering?
choices: It minimizes the sum of squared distances
It maximizes the number of clusters
It balances between minimizing the sum of squared distances and avoiding overfitting.
